skill.name: CRUD with Spec-Kit
skill.description: Guide AI-assisted teams through specification-driven CRUD implementation using Spec-Kit and Claude Code.
skill.summary: Plan, scaffold, and validate CRUD features from Spec-Kit specifications.
skill.author: Claude

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual review found no prompt-injection text, data-exfiltration intent, or executable behavior requiring remediation.

content.value_statement: CRUD work often drifts from written requirements. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code turn Spec-Kit files into aligned implementation plans.
actual_capabilities: Interprets Spec-Kit feature files for entities, fields, relationships, operations, and constraints.
Maps entity requirements to REST endpoints, request models, response formats, and error handling.
Plans frontend clients, data models, service layers, forms, and list views for CRUD workflows.
Checks implementations against success criteria, validation rules, and expected API formats.
Guides test planning for unit, integration, and validation coverage based on the specification.
limitations: It is a conceptual workflow guide and does not include executable scaffolding scripts.
It depends on complete Spec-Kit files with clear entities, operations, constraints, and success criteria.
It is not designed for complex business logic beyond standard CRUD behavior.
Generated implementation details still require review in the target framework and codebase.

use_cases.title: Generate CRUD API Plans
use_cases.description: Convert a Spec-Kit feature into a route, validation, and response plan before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Align Frontend Clients
use_cases.description: Create matching client services, data models, and UI component plans from backend entity requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Specification Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare implemented CRUD behavior against success criteria, validation rules, and expected response formats.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize CRUD Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Spec-Kit feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this Spec-Kit feature file and list the entities, required CRUD operations, validation rules, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Backend Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this specification, create a backend CRUD plan with routes, request fields, response shapes, status codes, and error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design Frontend Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Build client behavior from the API plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a frontend implementation plan for these CRUD endpoints, including data models, service methods, forms, lists, loading states, and validation feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Validate End-to-End Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this implementation against the Spec-Kit requirements. Identify missing CRUD behavior, validation gaps, response mismatches, and tests to add.

output_examples.input: A Spec-Kit file describes a Project entity with name, owner, status, and due date fields.
output_examples.output: A route plan for create, list, detail, update, and delete operations, plus validation rules for required fields and date handling.

output_examples.input: A team has backend routes and needs a matching frontend workflow for task management.
output: Client service methods for each operation.
A list view with filtering and empty states.
Create and edit form behavior with validation feedback.

output_examples.input: An existing CRUD implementation must be checked against success criteria.
output_examples.output: A coverage report that highlights implemented features, missing validation, response format differences, and recommended tests.

best_practices: Start with complete Spec-Kit files that define entities, fields, relationships, constraints, and success criteria.
Review generated plans against the target framework before writing production code.
Validate backend behavior, frontend client behavior, and tests against the same specification.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill when requirements are still changing rapidly.
Do not treat generated plans as production-ready code without review.
Do not use it for workflows that need complex domain rules outside standard CRUD.

faq.question: Does this skill generate working code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides AI-assisted planning, scaffolding, and validation. The final code depends on the selected framework and repository.

faq.question: What input does the skill need?
faq.answer: It needs Spec-Kit feature files with entities, fields, operations, constraints, expected responses, and success criteria.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude Code workflows and is also tagged for Claude and Codex compatibility.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-REST APIs?
faq.answer: It focuses on REST-style CRUD workflows. Other API styles may require manual adaptation.

faq.question: How should teams verify the output?
faq.answer: Compare every planned route, client method, validation rule, and test against the specification success criteria.

faq.question: What projects are a poor fit?
faq.answer: Projects with unclear specifications, non-standard data access, or complex business logic are a poor fit.
